jsonld.name: 401(k) Calculator
jsonld.description: Project a 401(k) balance at retirement with employer matching, annual raises and 2026 IRS contribution limits including age-based catch-up contributions.

mainEntity.name: Should I contribute enough to get the full employer match?

acceptedAnswer.text: Generally yes — an employer match is effectively free money, and missing it is one of the most common ways people leave value on the table. The callout under your projected balance shows how much match you're capturing.

mainEntity.name: Does this account for contribution limits?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Your contributions are capped at the 2026 IRS limit for your age each year: $24,500 under 50, $32,500 from 50 (with the $8,000 catch-up) and $35,750 at ages 60–63.

mainEntity.name: What happens if I leave my job — can I keep my 401(k)?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes — you can typically leave it with your former employer's plan, roll it into your new employer's plan, or roll it into an IRA, each with different pros and cons worth researching.

Traditional contributions reduce taxable income now with taxes owed on withdrawal; Roth contributions are taxed now but grow tax-free. The better choice often depends on whether you expect to be in a higher or lower tax bracket in retirement.

mainEntity.name: What happens to my employer match if I leave my job?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on your plan's vesting schedule — some employers require a certain number of years of service before you fully own matched contributions, so check your specific plan documents.

mainEntity.name: Is there a penalty for withdrawing from a 401(k) early?

acceptedAnswer.text: Withdrawals before age 59½ generally incur a 10% early withdrawal penalty on top of ordinary income tax, with some exceptions for specific circumstances — early withdrawal is generally discouraged given the impact on long-term growth.

mainEntity.name: How much will my employer match add over time?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the formula and your salary. At $70,000, a 50% match up to 6% pays $2,100 a year when you save 6%, and a 100% match up to 4% pays $2,800 a year. Use the Employer Match Structure box to project the total over your career.

mainEntity.name: What is the 2026 combined 401(k) contribution limit?

acceptedAnswer.text: The IRS limit on total additions to your account from you and your employer is $72,000 for 2026, not counting catch-up contributions. Your own deferral limit is $24,500 for most workers.

mainEntity.name: Do I have to make Roth catch-up contributions?

acceptedAnswer.text: If your prior-year FICA wages from your employer were above $150,000, your 2026 catch-up contributions must be Roth, provided your plan offers a Roth option. Lower earners can choose pre-tax or Roth catch-ups if the plan allows.

mainEntity.name: How do I see my 401(k) balance in today's dollars?

acceptedAnswer.text: Divide the projected balance by (1 + inflation) raised to the number of years, or enter your expected return minus inflation. For example, $1.51 million after 35 years at 3% inflation is worth about $537,000 in today's dollars.

mainEntity.name: How do I roll over my 401(k) to an IRA without paying tax?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ask for a direct rollover, so the money goes straight to the IRA. If a check is paid to you instead, 20% is withheld and you must replace it from other funds within 60 days to roll over the full amount.
